name: mono-color
description: Generate original one-ink or controlled two-ink editorial images from any theme, sentence, article idea, object, or reference photo. Always use this skill when the user asks for 单色海报、双色印刷、单色调视觉、蓝色/绿色孔版印刷、risograph、网点照片、复古或当代编辑排版、zine poster, monochrome editorial poster, duotone p

name: sepia
description: Review and revise prose while preserving facts and your voice. Includes writing, minimal edits, full rewrites, professional documents, fiction, and Chinese-language guidance.
example_prompt: Review my draft, then suggest minimal edits that preserve facts and my voice.
expected_output: A prose review or revised draft.
requirements: The text to revise and its intended audience.

name: internal-comms
description: Draft team updates, project reports, company newsletters, and FAQs using practical communication templates.
example_prompt: Turn my project notes into a weekly team update with progress, plans, and problems.
expected_output: A structured team update, newsletter, or FAQ.
requirements: Project notes and the intended audience.

name: theme-factory
description: Give slides, documents, and reports a consistent visual style with ten ready-made color and font themes or a custom theme.
example_prompt: Show me the available themes, then apply my choice to this presentation.
expected_output: A document or deck with consistent colors and typography.
requirements: An existing document or deck and file-editing tools.

name: content-research-writer
description: Research, outline, and refine articles with sources and section-by-section feedback.
example_prompt: Write a sourced briefing on the topic in my notes. Separate supported claims from open questions.
expected_output: A sourced outline and article draft.
requirements: Source notes and web search for claims needing verification.

name: meeting-insights-analyzer
description: Review meeting transcripts for communication patterns and specific, evidence-backed feedback.
example_prompt: Review this meeting transcript for unclear decisions and missed opportunities to listen. Quote the supporting passages.
expected_output: A feedback report with transcript excerpts and practical next steps.
requirements: A meeting transcript with speaker labels; recordings must be transcribed first.

name: changelog-generator
description: Turn a project’s Git history into clear release notes grouped by user impact.
example_prompt: Draft release notes from the commits between the two versions I specify. Explain changes in plain language.
expected_output: Draft release notes linked to the relevant changes.
requirements: Read access to a Git repository and the version range to summarize.

name: tailored-resume-generator
description: Tailor a resume to a job description using relevant experience and achievements.
example_prompt: Adapt my resume to this job description. Use only my actual experience and flag missing information.
expected_output: A tailored resume draft and a list of gaps to clarify.
requirements: Your existing resume and the target job description.

name: copy-editing
description: Improve existing copy through focused passes for clarity, consistency, and a stronger message.
example_prompt: Edit this announcement for clarity and concision. Preserve the facts and voice, and explain important edits.
expected_output: Edited copy with a concise explanation of changes.
requirements: The original draft and, optionally, brand or audience guidance.

name: diagram-design
description: Draw clean, restrained diagrams as HTML and SVG: flowcharts, conceptual frameworks, timelines, org charts, funnels, Venn diagrams and 30 more. Can match your brand colors and redraw an existing Mermaid or draw.io sketch.
example_prompt: Turn my conceptual model (trust leads to intention, moderated by risk) into a clean framework figure for my paper.
expected_output: An HTML or SVG diagram, optionally a PNG.
requirements: A description or rough sketch of what the diagram should show.

name: field-onboarding
description: Learn an unfamiliar research field step by step, from why it matters to its open questions, checking your understanding before moving on. Also explains a paper, figure or referee comment you cannot follow, and marks which works it cited from memory.
example_prompt: I am new to causal inference. Walk me into the field, starting from what I already know about experiments.
expected_output: A guided explanation, one step at a time, with a reading path.
requirements: A field, paper or comment you want to understand.

name: statistical-power
description: Work out how many participants a study needs: power analysis for t-tests, ANOVA, proportions, correlations and regression, minimum detectable effects, power curves, and simulation for more complex designs.
example_prompt: How many participants do I need per condition for a 2x2 between-subjects experiment with a small-to-medium effect?
expected_output: A sample-size justification with the calculation shown.
requirements: The planned design and an expected effect size.

name: experimental-design
description: Plan an experiment before collecting data: choose a design, randomize, block or stratify, and lay out the conditions so the results can be interpreted.
example_prompt: Help me design an online experiment testing two ad messages across three product categories.
expected_output: A study design with assignment plan and conditions.
requirements: The research question and practical constraints.

name: peer-review
description: Draft a careful, constructive peer review of a manuscript or proposal: check claims against evidence, methods, statistics and reporting guidelines. Asks you to confirm you are authorized to review before it reads anything.
example_prompt: Review this manuscript I was invited to review and draft my report to the editor.
expected_output: A structured review report.
requirements: The manuscript and the journal's review criteria, if any.

name: communication-construct
description: Before measuring something, check whether the concept already exists under another name, separate it from look-alike concepts, and lock one definition to use throughout the paper.
example_prompt: I want to study 'AI trust anxiety'. Does this construct already exist, and how should I define it?
expected_output: A construct definition with overlapping concepts sorted out.
requirements: The concept you want to study.

name: communication-scale
description: Find validated measurement scales, review their reliability and validity evidence, and plan translation or cross-cultural adaptation with measurement invariance checks.
example_prompt: Find a validated scale for perceived message credibility that I can use in a Chinese sample.
expected_output: Candidate scales with their evidence and an adaptation plan.
requirements: The construct to measure and the target population.

name: literature-monitor
description: Watch a fixed list of journals for newly published articles on your topic and produce a deduplicated digest. Only counts an article once it is actually visible on the publisher's site within your time window.
example_prompt: Every Monday, check Journal of Marketing, JCR and JMR for new papers on AI and consumer trust from the past week.
expected_output: A digest of new articles with verified titles and links.
requirements: The topic, journal list, schedule and time window.

name: course-audit
description: Audit a lecture, syllabus or assignment from the student's side: what it is for, what is actually in it, and which tasks a student could now finish with AI in five minutes. Reports numbered findings, and labels each as measured, inferred or assumed.
example_prompt: Audit my lecture slides on pricing strategy and tell me what to improve.
expected_output: A numbered list of findings you can accept or reject.
requirements: The teaching material (slides, PDF, syllabus or assignment).

name: course-rebuild
description: Act on a course audit: propose concrete changes, such as activities students actually answer, practice datasets that rotate each year, or new cases, then build only the ones you choose.
example_prompt: Take findings 2 and 5 from the audit and turn them into in-class activities.
expected_output: Revised teaching material and new activities.
requirements: A course audit, or the lecture you want to change.

name: timed-talk
description: Build a talk that fits a hard time limit: a word budget per slide, speaker notes with the exact words to say, and the timing measured rather than guessed. Marks which slides to cut if you run long.
example_prompt: I have a 12-minute conference slot. Build the talk and speaker notes from my paper so it fits.
expected_output: A timed talk outline with speaker notes and a cut list.
requirements: The content and the length of the slot.

name: lecture-deck
description: Build an animated HTML deck for a live class or workshop from a storyboard: one idea per screen, a strip showing whether the room is in slides, breakout or solo work, and speaker notes that carry the lecture.
example_prompt: Build a 90-minute workshop deck on customer journey mapping with two breakout sessions.
expected_output: An HTML deck with speaker notes.
requirements: A topic and session plan; Python for building the deck.

name: action-title-writer
description: Rewrite slide titles that only name a topic into full-sentence titles that state the takeaway, so the titles alone carry the argument.
example_prompt: Rewrite the titles in my deck so each one states its main point.
expected_output: Revised slide titles.
requirements: An existing deck or list of slide titles.

name: ghost-deck-skeleton
description: Sketch a deck as empty slides with takeaway titles and placeholders for charts, so the storyline is agreed before any time goes into design.
example_prompt: Before we design anything, sketch the storyline for a board update on our Q3 results.
expected_output: A skeleton deck with titles and placeholders.
requirements: The goal of the deck and the key findings.

name: reading-a-book
description: Read a book, long report or paper for real understanding, not a skim: classify it, map its structure, work through its arguments, and write notes as it goes so nothing is lost.
example_prompt: Read this book on consumer behavior carefully and give me notes I can use for my course.
expected_output: Structured reading notes.
requirements: The book or document.

name: literature-quick-review-note-en
description: Turn an academic paper into a condensed reading note as a Word document, with real margin comments that point to related literature.
example_prompt: Make a quick-review reading note of this paper as a Word file.
expected_output: A Word document with margin comments.
requirements: The paper as a PDF; Python for building the document.

name: attribution
description: Work out which marketing actually drives conversions: choose and read attribution models, reconcile conflicting numbers across tools, and plan incrementality or geo-lift tests.
example_prompt: Google Ads and our analytics tool disagree on conversions. Help me figure out which channel is really working.
expected_output: An attribution analysis and a testing plan.
requirements: Channel and conversion data, or a description of your setup.

name: ai-seo
description: Make content easier for AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews to find and cite: structure, sources, llms.txt and how to check whether you are being cited.
example_prompt: Review our product page and tell me how to make it more likely to be cited in AI answers.
expected_output: An audit with prioritized changes.
requirements: The page or content to review.
